feedback: D1: You catalogued 9 of the 10 findings with OWASP classes, CWEs, and reconciled evidence, which is solid work. The SQLi (A03/CWE-89, login.php, log 02:15:31), no-expiry JWT (CWE-613), stored XSS (CWE-79, log 02:18:47), path traversal (CWE-22, log 02:24:02), open redirect (CWE-601), and missing cookie flags (CWE-614) were all well evidenced. Two things cost you: you missed the XXE finding entirely (the 04-import-xxe.xml payload with SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd via import.php), and your weak-secret finding only said the signatures match "standard automated testing patterns" instead of quoting the actual hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, so it reads as half-proven. Your decoy call is wrong: the safe construct in this pack is the HS256 verify branch using hash_equals(), which is constant-time and sound, not the MD5 routine. MD5 is a genuine vulnerability you correctly listed as finding 2, so it cannot also be the decoy, and you needed to name hash_equals and prove it safe at the mechanism level. To your credit you did NOT mislabel alg:none as the decoy, which many people get wrong. D2: Your chain only has 3 hops (SQLi, the 312-row PII pull at 02:16:04, file read at 02:24:02) and skips the stored-XSS and open-redirect hops and the parallel XXE read, so the sequence is about half complete. The curl PoCs per hop are good. Your CVSS for the auth bypass, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N = 10.0, over-scales it: the login bypass itself is S:U and A:N giving roughly 9.1, and S:C belongs to the senior insight that a forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which you did not surface. Your impact named 312 customers but the 3,648,113.55 NGN figure undercounts badly; individual balances run up to about 950k NGN and the total reaches tens of millions tied to BoltCash in about 6 weeks, and you should state that assumption rather than a single low number. D3: This is where the most marks slipped. There is no executive summary at all, so the jargon-free customers-and-naira headline (6 pts) and the threat model (4 pts) both score zero. Your remediation matrix ordered by effort with a risk-reduction-per-hour column is exactly right and earned strong credit, and you correctly named Hop 1 SQLi parameterization as the earliest break. You only gave one detection stopgap (the SQLi tautology regex at 0.00% FP), and the row needs two with exact field and false-positive rate each. The disproved-decoy restatement is marked low because it disproves the wrong construct. D4: Good ethics work. You cited ISC2 Canons 2, 3, and 4 by number in a load-bearing way and tied NDPA Section 40 (72-hour NDPC notification) to the breach, and you anchored to login.php line 15 in your own voice. To go higher, cover all four prompts distinctly, including the single action you would take regardless of your manager, and add NDPA Section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects on high risk. I looked hard for a defensible way to push this over the line and could not get there honestly: the absent executive summary, absent threat model, missing XXE finding, and missing second detection rule are real gaps, not formatting quibbles, and I already credited your slightly-off CWE-327 as a class variant and gave benefit of the doubt on the naira and decoy rows. The single most important fix is to write a real executive summary that opens jargon-free and ends on a headline of 312 customers and tens of millions of naira, because that one section alone is worth 6 points and frames the whole report for the people who decide on the bounty.
